claims.text: Azathioprine: aminosalicylates (eg, sulfasalazine, mesalamine) inhibit TPMT in vitro, so combine with caution;
claims.quote: There is in vitro evidence that aminosalicylate derivatives (e.g., sulphasalazine, mesalazine, or olsalazine) inhibit the TPMT enzyme. Concomitant use of these agents with IMURAN should be done with caution.

claims.text: ACE inhibitors have been reported to induce anemia and severe leukopenia;
claims.quote: The use of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors to control hypertension in patients on azathioprine has been reported to induce anemia and severe leukopenia.

claims.text: it may inhibit warfarin's anticoagulant effect.
claims.quote: IMURAN may inhibit the anticoagulant effect of warfarin.

claims.text: Azathioprine: CBC with platelets weekly during the first month, twice monthly for the second and third months, then monthly (or more often with dose changes).
claims.quote: Patients on IMURAN should have complete blood counts, including platelet counts, weekly during the first month, twice monthly for the second and third months of treatment, then monthly or more frequently if dosage alterations or other therapy changes are necessary.

claims.text: TPMT or NUDT15 deficiency may raise the risk of severe, life-threatening myelotoxicity with conventional doses;
claims.quote: Patients with thiopurine S-methyl transferase (TPMT) or nucleotide diphosphatase (NUDT15) deficiency may be at an increased risk of severe and life-threatening myelotoxicity if receiving conventional doses of IMURAN

claims.text: consider alternative therapy if homozygous deficient and reduced doses if heterozygous.
claims.quote: Consider alternative therapy in patients with homozygous TPMT or NUDT15 deficiency and reduced dosages in patients with heterozygous deficiency

claims.text: Tell patients about the malignancy risk (lymphoma and other cancers, particularly of the skin) and to limit sun and UV exposure;
claims.quote: Patients receiving immunosuppressants, including IMURAN, are at increased risk of developing lymphoma and other malignancies, particularly of the skin. Physicians should inform patients of the risk of malignancy with IMURAN. As usual for patients with increased risk for skin cancer, exposure to sunlight and ultraviolet light should be limited

claims.text: it can cause fetal harm, so avoid it in pregnancy whenever possible.
claims.quote: IMURAN can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. IMURAN should not be given during pregnancy without careful weighing of risk versus benefit. Whenever possible, use of IMURAN in pregnant patients should be avoided.
